module_intro: Module 8 walked through a trading day session by session (Asia, London, New York) and showed how each session's behavior connects to the one before it. This module gives that daily story a formal name and reusable template: the Power of 3, or AMD (Accumulation, Manipulation, Distribution). Covers each phase individually, then unifies them into PO3 -- including its most emphasized property: this three-phase shape is fractal, appearing at every timeframe from a single candle up through an entire trading quarter. Closes by explicitly mapping the template onto Module 8's sessions.
prerequisites_stated_in_text: Builds on Module 3 (Market Structure Shift), Module 4 (Liquidity), and Module 8 (sessions, Judas Swing).
module_objectives: describe the accumulation phase and explain why it should be marked and observed rather than traded
describe the manipulation phase and explain its direct relationship to the liquidity sweep (Module 4) and Judas Swing (Module 8) concepts
describe the distribution phase and the specific lower-timeframe confirmation (a Market Structure Shift) used before entering it
explain what it means for the Power of 3 template to be described as fractal, with an example at two different timeframes
map the Asian, London, and New York sessions from Module 8 onto the Accumulation, Manipulation, and Distribution phases
explain why ICT-focused sources describe PO3 as descriptive rather than mechanical, and why the pattern does not appear identically on every single trading day

concepts.name: Accumulation
concepts.definition: Accumulation is the first phase of the Power of 3 (AMD) model, in which price consolidates within a relatively tight, horizontal range around the period's opening price while institutional participants are understood to build positions gradually, without yet producing a significant directional move.
concepts.ict_specific_meaning:
ICT-focused teaching, attributed throughout to Michael J. Huddleston, treats accumulation as the setup phase of a repeatable three-part daily (and, fractally, weekly, monthly, and quarterly) cycle. During this phase, price is described as ranging near the period's open, building a defined high and low, while large positions are built gradually enough to avoid moving price sharply against the participant doing the buying or selling.

This phase directly reuses the liquidity concepts from Module 4: as retail traders place orders at the obvious range boundaries and protective stops just beyond them, ICT-focused sources describe this as "charging" a pool of buy-side liquidity above the range and sell-side liquidity below it - liquidity the next phase (Manipulation) is expected to draw from.

Sources are consistent that accumulation is a phase to observe and mark, not trade - entering a position based on price bouncing within this range is described across multiple sources as a common and largely avoidable beginner error.
concepts.beginner_explanation: At the very start of a new trading period - a new day, a new week, or even a fresh session - price often doesn't do very much for a while. It drifts sideways in a fairly narrow band around wherever it opened. Accumulation is simply the name for this quiet opening stretch, during which (according to this framework) large participants are gradually building positions without yet tipping their hand about which direction the period will ultimately move.
detection_criteria: Note the period's opening price (a new day, week, or session, depending on the timeframe being analyzed).
Observe whether price consolidates in a relatively tight, roughly horizontal range near that opening price, rather than trending strongly in either direction.
Mark the high and low of this observed range as the accumulation range.
Resist entering trades based purely on price moving within this range; treat this phase as observational.
concepts.numeric_or_narrative_example:
Daily open at 100. Price ranges between 98 and 102 for the first several hours of the day.

This 98 - 102 band, formed shortly after the day's open and without a clear directional break in either direction, is the accumulation range. A trader following this framework would mark 98 and 102 as reference levels and would not yet take a position based on this observed ranging behavior alone.
concepts.what_it_tells_the_trader:
Accumulation tells the trader that the period has not yet revealed its intended direction, and provides two specific, markable reference levels (the range high and low) that the next phase is expected to interact with.

It does not tell the trader which direction the period will ultimately move, nor does the mere presence of a range guarantee that a clean Manipulation and Distribution sequence will follow - some periods simply continue ranging, or trend directly from the open without any distinct accumulation phase at all.
concepts.common_pairings_narrative: Accumulation is, on the daily timeframe, most commonly mapped directly onto the Asian session from Module 8 - the same range-building behavior described there is simply being reframed here as the first act of a named three-part cycle that also includes what happens afterward.

framework_placement.comes_before: Requires Buy-Side/Sell-Side Liquidity (Module 4) and Asian Session (Module 8).

beginner_mistakes_or_misinterpretations: Entering trades based on price movement within the accumulation range itself.
Assuming every period will produce a clean, easily identifiable accumulation range - some periods trend immediately from the open with no meaningful consolidation phase.
Forgetting to mark the range's high and low clearly before the next phase begins.
concepts.qualification_or_limits: Not every trading period features a clean, well-defined accumulation phase. Multiple sources explicitly note that the full three-phase pattern appears with "remarkable consistency but not every single day," and that on days with major scheduled news or unusually low volatility, this phase may be compressed, disrupted, or difficult to trade even when it is present.

completetradersedge.com - "The ICT Power of 3: Accumulation, Manipulation, Distribution" (explicit acknowledgment the pattern does not appear every single day).

concepts.name: Manipulation
concepts.definition: Manipulation is the second phase of the Power of 3 model, in which price is deliberately (from the institutional perspective this framework describes) pushed beyond one boundary of the accumulation range - triggering resting stop-loss and breakout orders - before reversing into the period's true intended direction.
concepts.ict_specific_meaning:
ICT-focused sources describe this phase as functionally identical to the Judas Swing concept introduced in Module 8: a false move beyond the accumulation range, engineered (in this framework's narrative) to trap breakout traders and trigger the stop-losses of traders who had positioned within the range, thereby providing the liquidity institutions are described as needing to complete their positioning.

The direction of the manipulation move is consistently described as opposite to the period's eventual true direction: in a bullish period, manipulation drives price below the accumulation range low (a bear trap); in a bearish period, manipulation drives price above the accumulation range high (a bull trap).

Multiple sources frame this phase as deliberately exploiting predictable retail trading psychology - impulsiveness, a tendency to chase breakouts, and a tendency to panic-exit on adverse moves - a narrative framing this book presents descriptively, as it appears across ICT-focused sources, rather than as an independently verified claim about institutional intent.
concepts.beginner_explanation: After a quiet opening range, manipulation is the moment things suddenly seem to break out - price shoots beyond the top or bottom of that range, and it looks like the "real" move has finally started. According to this framework, that appearance is precisely the trap: this initial break is not actually the period's true direction, but a deliberate detour designed to catch traders leaning the wrong way before the market reverses.
detection_criteria: Confirm an accumulation range has already been established (see Accumulation).
Watch for price to break beyond one boundary of that range - above the high or below the low.
Assess whether this break appears to be triggering an unusually sharp, brief spike (consistent with a stop-run) rather than a sustained, steadily building move.
Watch for signs of reversal shortly after the break - this is what would subsequently confirm the move as manipulation rather than a genuine breakout (see Distribution, next).
concepts.numeric_or_narrative_example:
Accumulation range: 98 - 102. Price spikes down to 95, then reverses back up through 102.

The spike down to 95 - briefly piercing below the accumulation range low of 98 before reversing - is the manipulation move. Under this framework, this move is read as an engineered dip designed to trigger sell-stop orders and lure in breakout sellers, immediately before the period's true (in this example, bullish) direction asserts itself.
concepts.what_it_tells_the_trader:
Manipulation tells the trader that a specific liquidity pool (one side of the accumulation range) has likely been targeted and triggered, and - once confirmed by a reversal - offers a strong contextual clue about the period's true intended direction (generally opposite to the manipulation move itself).

It does not, while still in progress, tell the trader with certainty that a reversal will follow; a move that continues past the expected reversal point, without reversing, is instead a genuine breakout, not manipulation - the same distinction already introduced for the Judas Swing in Module 8.
concepts.common_pairings_narrative: Manipulation is, in every meaningful respect, the same event as the liquidity sweep and Judas Swing concepts from Modules 4 and 8, renamed here as the middle act of the broader three-phase cycle that also formally includes the accumulation setup before it and the distribution payoff after it.
beginner_mistakes_or_misinterpretations: Chasing the initial manipulation move as though it were the period's genuine direction.
Failing to wait for confirmation (displacement and a structure shift) that the reversal is actually underway before acting.
concepts.qualification_or_limits: Manipulation, like the Judas Swing it mirrors, cannot be distinguished from a genuine breakout with certainty until after the fact. A move beyond the accumulation range that fails to reverse within a reasonable number of candles should be treated as a real breakout, not manipulation.

concepts.name: Distribution
concepts.definition: Distribution is the third and final phase of the Power of 3 model, in which price reverses out of the Manipulation move and delivers the period's genuine, sustained directional move, typically targeting the liquidity resting on the opposite side of the original accumulation range and beyond.
concepts.ict_specific_meaning:
ICT-focused sources consistently describe distribution as the only phase of the three that is actually intended to be traded - accumulation is for marking, manipulation is for confirming and identifying direction, and distribution is where a position is actually opened and managed.

Multiple sources describe the ideal, cautious sequencing for entering a distribution move: wait for the accumulation range to complete, watch the manipulation phase happen without acting on it, and only enter once a lower-timeframe confirmation - commonly a Change of Character or Market Structure Shift (Module 3) - confirms the reversal out of the manipulation extreme is genuinely underway. This approach means missing the very first portion of the move in exchange for a meaningfully more confirmed, better-defined entry.

On a completed candle (of any timeframe - daily, weekly, or otherwise), sources describe the distribution phase as visually corresponding to the candle's "body": the wick represents the manipulation excursion, and the larger, sustained move back toward (and beyond) the open represents distribution, which is why a completed bullish PO3 period is commonly described as opening near its low, wicking below the open, and closing near its high (with the mirror pattern for a bearish period).
concepts.beginner_explanation: After the deceptive manipulation move reverses, distribution is simply the name for what happens next: the actual, sustained move in the period's true direction - the part of the day (or week, or any other period) where the majority of genuine, lasting price movement occurs, and where this framework says the real trading opportunity exists.
detection_criteria: Confirm a manipulation move has occurred and appears to be reversing (see Manipulation).
Watch for a lower-timeframe confirmation of this reversal - commonly a Market Structure Shift (Module 3).
Enter in the direction of this confirmed reversal, rather than during the manipulation move itself.
Target the liquidity resting on the opposite side of the original accumulation range, and beyond, as the objective for this move.
concepts.numeric_or_narrative_example:
Accumulation range: 98 - 102. Manipulation: spike to 95, reversal begins. Distribution: price rallies from 95 through 102 and continues to 115.

The sustained rally from 95 through 102 and on to 115 is the distribution phase - the period's genuine, sustained directional move, reversing the manipulation dip and ultimately targeting (and exceeding) the buy-side liquidity resting above the original accumulation range high of 102.
concepts.what_it_tells_the_trader:
Distribution tells the trader that the period's true intended direction has been confirmed and is now actively developing, providing the specific window during which an entry, according to this framework, should actually be taken.

It does not tell the trader exactly how far the distribution move will travel, or guarantee that it will reach every candidate liquidity target beyond the original range - targets remain probabilistic, as described throughout Module 4.
concepts.common_pairings_narrative: Distribution is confirmed using the exact same Market Structure Shift concept from Module 3, and it is the phase most directly identified, on the daily timeframe, with the New York session from Module 8 - the session ICT-focused sources describe as delivering the day's main expansion.

framework_placement.comes_before: Requires Manipulation and Market Structure Shift (Module 3).
framework_placement.comes_after: Concludes the three-phase cycle and feeds into Power of 3 (the consolidated concept) and Session Relationship to PO3.

beginner_mistakes_or_misinterpretations: Entering during the manipulation phase rather than waiting for confirmed distribution.
Exiting a distribution-phase trade prematurely, before it has reached a reasonable liquidity target, out of a lack of confidence in the move.
Assuming every manipulation move is immediately followed by clean, uninterrupted distribution, rather than allowing for a period of consolidation or partial retracement along the way.
concepts.qualification_or_limits: Distribution describes the expected outcome once accumulation and manipulation have both been correctly identified, but this book, echoing sources reviewed for this module, is explicit that the full three-phase pattern does not appear on every single trading day, and that entering purely on the expectation of distribution, without a genuine lower-timeframe confirmation, undermines the entire discipline the model is meant to encourage.

concepts.name: Power of 3 (PO3)
concepts.definition: The Power of 3 (PO3), also referred to as the AMD model, is the complete, named three-phase template - Accumulation, Manipulation, Distribution - that ICT-focused teaching uses to describe how a trading period of any length (a session, a day, a week, a month, or a quarter) tends to unfold around its opening price.
concepts.ict_specific_meaning:
ICT-focused sources, attributing the model directly to Michael J. Huddleston, describe PO3 as one of the most fundamental organizing concepts in the entire framework - several sources go as far as calling it the "master framework" that every other ICT concept (Kill Zones, liquidity sweeps, Fair Value Gaps, Order Blocks, Market Structure Shifts) is understood to operate inside of, rather than a separate, standalone tool.

The single most emphasized property of PO3 across every source reviewed is that it is fractal: the identical three-phase shape is described as appearing simultaneously at every scale - a single candle's own open-high-low-close anatomy, an intraday session, a full trading day, a trading week, and even a full month or quarter, with each larger scale's phases containing a complete, nested copy of the same pattern at the scale below it.
concepts.beginner_explanation: Power of 3 is the name for the whole three-part story this module has walked through in pieces: a quiet setup (Accumulation), a deceptive trap (Manipulation), and the real payoff (Distribution). What makes this idea especially powerful, according to ICT-focused teaching, is that this exact three-part story is said to repeat at almost every possible zoom level - from a single candle, to an hour, to a full day, to an entire week - like a pattern that looks the same no matter how far you zoom in or out.
detection_criteria: Choose the specific period being analyzed (a session, a day, a week, or another interval).
Identify that period's opening price.
Mark the Accumulation range that forms near that open.
Watch for the Manipulation move beyond one side of that range.
Confirm and act on the Distribution move that follows, once genuinely confirmed.

Recognize that this same template can, in principle, be found nested inside any single phase of a larger PO3 cycle - for example, a smaller, complete PO3 cycle occurring entirely within a larger cycle's manipulation phase.
concepts.numeric_or_narrative_example:
Weekly PO3: Monday - Tuesday accumulation (range 1000 - 1020), Tuesday - Wednesday manipulation (spike to 990), Thursday - Friday distribution (rally to 1080)

This single example illustrates the same three-phase shape already shown at the daily level earlier in this module, but stretched across an entire trading week rather than a single day - the specific mechanism (range, trap, payoff) is identical; only the timeframe and the specific price levels have changed.
concepts.what_it_tells_the_trader:
Power of 3 tells the trader a single, reusable mental template for organizing price behavior at any timeframe, and explains why this book's earlier modules (structure, liquidity, displacement, sessions) all fit together into one coherent story rather than being a disconnected list of separate tools.

It does not tell the trader that every period, at every timeframe, will always display a clean, tradable version of this pattern - as emphasized throughout this module, the pattern is descriptive of a common tendency, not a mechanical guarantee that repeats identically every single time.
concepts.common_pairings_narrative: Power of 3 is simply the named, unified version of the three individual phase concepts already covered in this module, and it directly sets up Module 10's Bias concept (since correctly reading which phase a period is currently in is a central input into establishing directional bias) and Module 13's full daily execution workflow.

framework_placement.comes_after: Feeds directly into Session Relationship to PO3, and later into Bias (Module 10) and Daily Trading & Scalping (Module 13).

beginner_mistakes_or_misinterpretations: Treating PO3 as a mechanical, guaranteed prediction tool rather than a descriptive template for organizing analysis.
Applying the model rigidly to every single timeframe and period without adjusting for that specific market's or instrument's typical behavior.
Losing track of which specific timeframe's PO3 cycle is currently being analyzed when multiple nested cycles are considered at once.
concepts.qualification_or_limits: PO3 is explicitly described across ICT-focused sources as descriptive rather than mechanical - a way of framing what could happen around a period's open, not a rule that produces a clean, tradable accumulation-manipulation-distribution sequence in every period, on every instrument, at every timeframe.

luxalgo.com - "Accumulation-manipulation-distribution - Smart Money Concepts / ICT Concept" (fractal property, explicit "descriptive, not mechanical" framing).

concepts.name: Session Relationship to PO3
concepts.definition: This concept maps the three PO3 phases directly onto the specific trading sessions covered in Module 8: on the daily timeframe, the Asian session typically corresponds to Accumulation, the London session (and specifically its opening hours) to Manipulation, and the New York session to Distribution.
concepts.ict_specific_meaning:
This mapping is described with strong consistency across ICT-focused sources as the single most common and most heavily taught application of PO3: rather than treating Accumulation, Manipulation, and Distribution as abstract phases identifiable only after the fact, this mapping gives a trader a specific, clock-based, repeatable daily routine for anticipating which phase is most likely occurring at any given moment.

Sources note that this mapping is a general tendency, not a rigid rule - some explicitly observe that London's open specifically (rather than the entire London session) is where the sharpest manipulation activity is concentrated, with the remainder of the London session and the New York session together forming the bulk of the eventual distribution move.

The same fractal principle from the previous concept applies here directly: this daily-level Asia/London/New York mapping is described as itself nesting inside a larger weekly mapping (for example, Monday - Tuesday accumulation, a midweek manipulation, and a Thursday - Friday distribution), which in turn nests inside monthly and quarterly versions of the same template.
concepts.beginner_explanation: Module 8 already introduced the idea that Asia tends to build a range, London tends to deliver a deceptive early move, and New York tends to deliver the day's real move. This concept simply gives that same observed pattern its formal name: Asia is Accumulation, London (especially its open) is Manipulation, and New York is Distribution - the entire daily session cycle from Module 8, read through the lens of the Power of 3 template from this module.
detection_criteria: Mark the Asian session's range as the day's Accumulation phase (Module 8's Asian Range).
Watch the London session's opening hours for the day's Manipulation move (Module 8's Judas Swing).
Watch the New York session for the day's Distribution move, confirmed by a Market Structure Shift.
Cross-check this daily-level reading against the same template applied to the current trading week, for additional (fractal) context.
concepts.numeric_or_narrative_example:
Asia (Accumulation): range 100 - 103. London Open (Manipulation): spike to 104.5, reversal. New York (Distribution): rally from 96 to 112.

This is the exact same worked sequence already introduced in Module 8's London Open Kill Zone example, now explicitly labeled using this module's vocabulary: the Asian range is the Accumulation phase, the London Open spike-and-reverse is the Manipulation phase, and the New York rally is the Distribution phase - one continuous daily story, told twice with two complementary vocabularies.
concepts.what_it_tells_the_trader:
This mapping tells the trader specifically when, during the trading day, to expect each PO3 phase to occur, turning the abstract three-phase template into an actionable daily schedule tied directly to the Kill Zones already covered in Module 8.

It does not tell the trader that this mapping holds with perfect reliability every single day - Module 8 already documented that a clean Judas Swing does not appear on every trading day, and the same caveat applies here: some days' true manipulation or distribution phases occur in a different session than this general mapping would predict.
concepts.common_pairings_narrative: This concept is the direct, explicit bridge between Module 8's session-by-session daily narrative and this module's formal three-phase vocabulary, and it is the specific mechanism by which a trader forms the daily bias formalized in the next module.

framework_placement.comes_before: Requires Power of 3 and all of Module 8 (Time & Trading Sessions).
framework_placement.comes_after: Concludes Module 9 and feeds directly into Module 10 (Bias), where correctly reading the current PO3 phase becomes one of the central inputs into establishing a daily directional expectation.

beginner_mistakes_or_misinterpretations: Assuming this session-to-phase mapping is a fixed, universal rule rather than a general tendency that can vary by instrument, by day, and by unusual news events.
Forgetting that the same fractal template also applies at the weekly and monthly level, and analyzing only the daily mapping in isolation.
concepts.qualification_or_limits: This specific session-to-phase mapping (Asia = Accumulation, London = Manipulation, New York = Distribution) is a widely and consistently taught application of PO3 within ICT-focused sources, but it remains a general tendency rather than a fixed law - on some days, the true manipulation or distribution phase may occur earlier, later, or within a different session than this general mapping predicts, particularly around major scheduled news events.

rules.statement: The Accumulation-Manipulation-Distribution (AMD) shape is fractal: it appears identically in shape (if not exact scale) inside a single candle, a trading session, a full day, a week, a month, and a quarter, with smaller cycles nesting inside the phases of larger ones (e.g., a smaller, complete PO3 cycle can occur entirely within a larger cycle's manipulation phase).
rules.exceptions_or_qualifiers: Descriptive tendency, not a rule guaranteeing a clean sequence in every period, on every instrument, at every timeframe.

rules.statement: A move beyond the accumulation range that fails to reverse within a reasonable number of candles should be treated as a real breakout, not manipulation.
rules.exceptions_or_qualifiers: Exact 'reasonable number of candles' unspecified (contrast with Module 8's Judas Swing, which specifies ~2-3 candles).

rules.statement: Session-to-phase mapping (daily timeframe): Asian session = Accumulation; London session (especially its opening hours) = Manipulation; New York session = Distribution. Cross-check the daily-level reading against the same template applied to the current trading week for additional fractal context.
rules.exceptions_or_qualifiers: A general tendency, not a fixed law -- the true manipulation or distribution phase may occur earlier, later, or in a different session, particularly around major scheduled news events.

strategies.name: Power of 3 (AMD) Daily Template

context.htf_bias_required: unspecified explicitly here (implied consistency with overall HTF bias from Module 2/10)
context.session_or_time: Any period with a defined opening price (session, day, week, month, quarter); commonly applied on the daily timeframe mapped to Asia/London/New York sessions.
context.other_context: Requires an identifiable opening price for the period being analyzed.

setup: Mark the Accumulation range: observe price consolidating in a relatively tight, roughly horizontal range near the open; mark the high/low of this range. Resist entering trades based purely on price moving within this range.
Watch for the Manipulation move: price breaks beyond one boundary of the accumulation range (an unusually sharp, brief spike consistent with a stop-run), then shows signs of reversing shortly after.
strategies.entry_condition: Enter in the direction of the confirmed Distribution reversal once a lower-timeframe confirmation (commonly a Market Structure Shift, Module 3) occurs -- not during the manipulation move itself.
strategies.invalidation_or_stop: If the move beyond the accumulation range fails to reverse within a reasonable number of candles, treat it as a genuine breakout rather than manipulation (i.e., the AMD read is invalidated / no Distribution-phase trade is taken under this model). Entering purely on the expectation of distribution, without genuine LTF confirmation, is explicitly discouraged.
strategies.target_or_exit: Target the liquidity resting on the opposite side of the original accumulation range, and beyond.
sequencing_steps_verbatim_order: Choose the specific period being analyzed.
Mark the Accumulation range that forms near that open.
Watch for the Manipulation move beyond one side of that range.
Confirm and act on the Distribution move that follows, once genuinely confirmed.
missing_elements: Exact stop-loss placement not restated here (deferred to Module 7 Entry Zone / Modules 11-12).
'Reasonable number of candles' for manipulation invalidation is not numerically defined here (contrast Module 8's Judas Swing ~2-3 candle rule).

relationships.statement:
This module builds a single, repeatable three-act story and then shows how far that story generalizes. Accumulation, Manipulation, and Distribution are the three individual phases, presented in the order they occur: a quiet range-building setup, a deceptive trap that reuses Module 4's liquidity sweep and Module 8's Judas Swing concepts under a new name, and a confirmed, tradable payoff move that reuses Module 3's Market Structure Shift as its confirmation tool.

Power of 3 then names the complete three-act template as a single, unified concept and introduces the property that makes it so central to ICT-focused teaching: it is fractal, appearing identically (in shape, if not in exact scale) inside a single candle, a trading session, a full day, a week, a month, and a quarter, with smaller cycles nesting inside the phases of larger ones. Session Relationship to PO3 closes the module by making the single most common practical application of this template explicit: on the daily timeframe, Asia is Accumulation, London (especially its open) is Manipulation, and New York is Distribution - directly relabeling Module 8's session narrative using this module's formal three-phase vocabulary.

no_trade_conditions.statement: Resist entering trades based purely on price moving within the accumulation range; treat the Accumulation phase as observational only.

Do not enter purely on the expectation of a distribution move without a genuine lower-timeframe confirmation (e.g., Market Structure Shift); doing so undermines the discipline the model is meant to encourage.

module_review_notes.beginner_summary: ICT-focused teaching describes a repeatable three-part story behind how a trading period tends to unfold around its opening price. First, Accumulation: price ranges quietly near the open while positions are built gradually, and traders following this framework mark this range without trading it. Second, Manipulation: price is pushed beyond one side of that range - the same event described elsewhere in this book as a liquidity sweep or Judas Swing - trapping traders leaning the wrong way before reversing. Third, Distribution: the period's real, sustained move develops in the opposite direction from the manipulation, confirmed by a Market Structure Shift, and this is the only phase of the three actually meant to be traded. Together these three phases are called the Power of 3, or AMD, and the single most important property of this template is that it is fractal - the same three-act shape is said to appear at every scale, from a single candle up through an entire trading quarter. On the daily timeframe specifically, this template is most commonly mapped directly onto Module 8's three sessions: Asia accumulates, London (especially its open) manipulates, and New York distributes.
module_review_notes.concept_relationships_summary: Accumulation, Manipulation, and Distribution are the three sequential phases. Power of 3 is the unified, named template combining all three and adding the fractal property. Session Relationship to PO3 is the specific, most commonly taught daily-timeframe application of that template, mapping it directly onto the Asian, London, and New York sessions from Module 8.
module_review_notes.practical_chart_exercise: Using the following weekly sequence - Monday - Tuesday: price ranges between 500 and 520; Wednesday: price spikes down to 485 before reversing; Thursday - Friday: price rallies to 560 - label each part of this sequence with its correct Power of 3 phase, identify the specific price levels a trader following this framework would have marked during the first phase, and explain what lower-timeframe confirmation you would want to see before treating the Wednesday reversal as the start of genuine distribution rather than continued manipulation.
self_test_questions: Why does ICT-focused teaching advise marking the accumulation range without trading it?
What is the relationship between the manipulation phase described in this module and the liquidity sweep and Judas Swing concepts from earlier modules?
What specific lower-timeframe confirmation tool is commonly used to confirm that distribution has genuinely begun, rather than the manipulation move simply continuing?
What does it mean to describe the Power of 3 template as "fractal"?
On the daily timeframe, which specific session is most commonly mapped to each of the three PO3 phases?
common_misconceptions: Believing the Power of 3 pattern appears identically, and with guaranteed reliability, on every single trading day, week, or other period.
Trading during the accumulation or manipulation phases directly, rather than treating them as observational and confirmatory steps leading up to a distribution-phase entry.
Believing the daily session mapping (Asia/London/New York) is a fixed, universal rule rather than a general, commonly observed tendency that can vary, particularly around major news events.

Treating PO3 as an entirely separate tool from the liquidity, structure, and session concepts covered in earlier modules, rather than recognizing it as a unifying template built directly on top of them.
